title: PolicyModel
description: A per-policy tier-2 experiment model: the assumptions a reader may set and the deterministic arithmetic PDI performs over real denominators. One file per policy at data/policies/models/<policy_id>.json. A policy with no such file has no tier 2, which is the normal state and is not an error. Every output of this file is a projection, never a finding, and never evidence that the policy caused anything.

unit.description: Closed unit vocabulary. percent_points is 0-100 and share is 0-1; they are separate members because a factor-of-100 error is invisible in a payload and obvious on a page only after someone has screenshotted it.

precision.description: Decimal places for display. Capped at 2 because pkg/grounding.Verify registers result values at 0, 1 and 2 decimals; a figure rendered at 3 would be rejected as unsupported in generated prose that quoted the page correctly.

i18n_key.description: An i18n key in this page's namespace, e.g. pex.param.snap_uptake.label. The model file carries keys, never display prose, so a Spanish reader is never shown an English string a backend author happened to write.

expr.description: One node of the model's arithmetic. The operation set is closed and no string is ever evaluated: the tree is the program. A closed set is what lets an unrepresentable model be refused instead of approximated, and it is what makes the projection taint provably total.

op.description: Node shape. ref and const are leaves; every other operation carries terms. sub subtracts every term after the first from the first; div divides the first by every term after it.

ref.description: A namespaced input reference. param:<id> resolves to a reader-set assumption (kind assumed); indicator:<variable_id> and reach:<field_id> resolve to loaded measured values; output:<id> resolves to an output declared EARLIER in this file. Forward and cyclic references are refused at load, not resolved at evaluation. Required when op is ref.

const.description: A literal value. Required when op is const.

const_kind.description: Classifies a literal. Defaults to assumed when omitted, which is the safe direction: an unclassified number typed into a JSON file is an assumption until a source says otherwise, and the failure mode of the other default is a projection that presents as a measurement. measured requires const_source.

const_source.description: Citation for a measured literal: publisher, document, figure. Required when const_kind is measured, because a published constant with nowhere to check it is an assumption wearing a source's clothes.

terms.description: Child terms. Required and non-empty for add, sub, mul, div, min and max; absent for ref and const.

term.description: A child of an operation, with the label the analyst register uses to show the arithmetic as a sentence a reader can check by hand. The trace is the argument: a projection with a hidden derivation asks for trust, one with a visible derivation asks for disagreement, which is the only useful thing a reader can do with an assumption.

label_key.description: i18n key naming this term in the arithmetic trace. Omitted means the term is rendered by its referent's own label.

schema_version.description: Model-file format version. A file declaring anything else is refused rather than best-effort parsed: the cost of a misread coefficient is a wrong number on a public page.

policy_id.description: Must match a record id in data/policies/*.csv AND the filename stem, so a mismatch is a load-time refusal rather than a file that quietly models the wrong policy.

model_version.description: Bumped whenever any expression, parameter bound or default changes. It travels in every evaluation result and every share link, so a link produced before a revision cannot silently render different numbers after one.

geo_levels.description: Geographic levels this model may be evaluated at. A request for any other level yields missing_reason geo_level_unsupported rather than an evaluation at a level the denominators do not support.

default_geoid.description: Geography used when the request carries none. The response always reports which geography it used and why, so a reader is never shown a default place they believe they asked for.

title_key.description: i18n key for this model's own name, as shown above the controls.

summary_key.description: i18n key for one sentence saying what this arithmetic is and is not.

params.description: The assumptions a reader sets, in display order. This is the only place a number enters the arithmetic that did not come from a dataset.

id.description: Stable, unique within this model. Also the linking key in comparison mode: two policies whose models declare the same id and the same unit are driven by one shared control.

label_key.description: i18n key for the control's label.

help_key.description: i18n key for the one-sentence explanation of what the reader is being asked to decide.

min.description: Lower bound. A submitted value below this is rejected with HTTP 400, never clamped: clamping silently substitutes a different assumption than the reader made and then attributes the result to them.

max.description: Upper bound. A submitted value above this is rejected with HTTP 400, never clamped.

step.description: Control granularity, and the grid a submitted value is canonicalised onto before it enters a cache key or a share link.

default.description: The position the control opens at. Authored by a human in this file; never derived from data and never proposed by a language model.

default_source_key.description: i18n key stating where the default came from: a published figure, or an explicitly arbitrary starting point. A default with no stated basis is a recommendation the page is making without admitting it.

outputs.description: The numbers this model produces, in declaration and evaluation order. An output:<id> reference may only name an earlier entry in this array.

id.description: Stable, unique within this model. Also the target of an output:<id> reference.

label_key.description: i18n key for the output's label.

unit.description: Declared, never inferred. The evaluator does no unit algebra: dividing dollars by people does not silently become usd_per_person. A mismatch between a declared unit and the arithmetic is caught by model lint at author time, where a person can fix it, rather than papered over at runtime where nobody sees it.

register.description: Disclosure layer this output first appears in. Public outputs are the two or three numbers the page is actually about; intermediate quantities belong in the analyst register. The analyst register is strictly additive: no figure changes value when a reader expands it.

refusal_keys.description: i18n keys for the specific things this model may not be read as saying - the sentences a reader would otherwise supply for themselves. Required and non-empty: a model that cannot name what it does not show has not been thought through.

caveat_keys.description: i18n keys for standing caveats on this model's inputs, such as a vintage collision between a designation and a population count.

authored_by.description: Who wrote the assumptions and the arithmetic.

reviewed_by.description: Who checked them. A model with no reviewer does not ship: the arithmetic is easy and the assumptions are the whole argument.
